queries.body_or_sql:
-- name: daily_supply_flows
-- description: End-of-day total supply and the gross mint and burn behind it, from the per-block change in blocks.total_supply (yoctoNEAR, FLOAT64) ordered by block_height. Supply only rises at epoch boundaries (validator and treasury reward mint) and only falls through burns, so positive deltas are summed as minted_near and negative deltas as burnt_near; the boundary block's own burn is netted into its mint. epoch_boundaries counts deltas above 10 NEAR. The query also reads @start_date - 1 so the first block of the range has a predecessor, then drops that day. A day whose first block has no predecessor in the previous calendar day (a gap in the table) gets empty mint, burn and boundary counts instead of a delta that spans the gap; genesis day 2020-07-21 is exempt. burnt_near is total supply destruction (fee burn net of the 30% contract reward, plus any other burn), not gross fees.
-- grain: one row per block_date
-- params: @start_date DATE, @end_date DATE (inclusive block_date range; the query reads block_date from @start_date - 1 for the LAG and drops that day)
-- est: 0.002 GB/day (blocks: block_date, block_height, total_supply = 24 bytes x ~78k blocks/day, DERIVED from the Nov 2024 table size; recent days are heavier, the dry run is authoritative)
WITH block_supply AS (
  SELECT
    block_date,
    block_height,
    CAST(total_supply AS FLOAT64) AS total_supply
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.crypto_near_mainnet_us.blocks`
  WHERE block_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(@start_date, INTERVAL 1 DAY) AND @end_date
),
deltas AS (
  SELECT
    block_date,
    block_height,
    total_supply,
    total_supply - LAG(total_supply) OVER chain AS supply_delta,
    LAG(block_date) OVER chain AS prev_block_date
  FROM block_supply
  WINDOW chain AS (ORDER BY block_height)
),
days AS (
  SELECT
    block_date,
    ARRAY_AGG(total_supply IGNORE NULLS ORDER BY block_height DESC LIMIT 1)[SAFE_OFFSET(0)] AS eod_supply,
    SUM(IF(supply_delta > 0, supply_delta, 0)) AS minted,
    SUM(IF(supply_delta < 0, -supply_delta, 0)) AS burnt,
    COUNTIF(supply_delta > 1e25) AS boundaries,
    LOGICAL_AND(
      block_date = DATE '2020-07-21'
      OR (supply_delta IS NOT NULL AND DATE_DIFF(block_date, prev_block_date, DAY) <= 1)
    ) AS deltas_complete
  FROM deltas
  WHERE block_date BETWEEN @start_date AND @end_date
  GROUP BY block_date
)
SELECT
  block_date,
  eod_supply / 1e24 AS eod_supply_near,
  IF(deltas_complete, minted / 1e24, NULL) AS minted_near,
  IF(deltas_complete, burnt / 1e24, NULL) AS burnt_near,
  IF(deltas_complete, boundaries, NULL) AS epoch_boundaries
FROM days
ORDER BY block_date

-- name: fee_burn
-- description: Gross fee burn and gas burnt per sampled day: execution_outcomes.tokens_burnt and gas_burnt (receipt execution) plus transactions.receipt_conversion_tokens_burnt and receipt_conversion_gas_burnt (transaction-to-receipt conversion), yoctoNEAR / 1e24 and gas / 1e12. Gross: until HSP-027 took effect (thesis/constants.toml hsp027_activation: first block with burnt_gas_reward 0, nearcore 2.14.0) nearcore recorded tokens_burnt before paying 30% of function-call gas to the called contract (runtime/src/lib.rs, burnt_gas_reward 3/10), so on days before that block this overstates the true supply burn; from that block the rebate is 0 and gross equals net. daily_supply_flows.burnt_near is the net throughout. Amount columns are cast to FLOAT64 because their stored types are only known from a Nov 2024 schema dump. A day missing from either table produces no row.
-- grain: one row per block_date
-- params: @start_date DATE, @end_date DATE (inclusive block_date range on both tables; the runner passes one sampled day or a contiguous run of sampled days within one month)
-- est: 0.19 GB/day (execution_outcomes: block_date, tokens_burnt, gas_burnt = 24 bytes x ~6.2M outcomes/day; transactions: block_date, receipt_conversion_tokens_burnt, receipt_conversion_gas_burnt = 24 bytes x ~1.75M tx/day; DERIVED from the Nov 2024 table sizes, recent days are heavier, the dry run is authoritative)
WITH outcomes AS (
  SELECT
    block_date,
    SUM(CAST(tokens_burnt AS FLOAT64)) AS tokens_burnt,
    SUM(CAST(gas_burnt AS FLOAT64)) AS gas_burnt
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.crypto_near_mainnet_us.execution_outcomes`
  WHERE block_date BETWEEN @start_date AND @end_date
  GROUP BY block_date
),
conversions AS (
  SELECT
    block_date,
    SUM(CAST(receipt_conversion_tokens_burnt AS FLOAT64)) AS tokens_burnt,
    SUM(CAST(receipt_conversion_gas_burnt AS FLOAT64)) AS gas_burnt
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.crypto_near_mainnet_us.transactions`
  WHERE block_date BETWEEN @start_date AND @end_date
  GROUP BY block_date
)
SELECT
  o.block_date,
  (o.tokens_burnt + c.tokens_burnt) / 1e24 AS gross_fee_burn_near,
  (o.gas_burnt + c.gas_burnt) / 1e12 AS gas_burnt_tgas
FROM outcomes AS o
INNER JOIN conversions AS c
  ON c.block_date = o.block_date
ORDER BY o.block_date

table.footnote: method names how burn_share_pct was measured. exact: every epoch boundary sums the mint at each boundary between the two 00:00 UTC samples (rpc/epoch_mints.csv, each row linked to the one before) and takes burnt as minted minus supply growth; epoch_boundaries counts them. sampled_share_pct: burnt over minted summed over one complete epoch per calendar month (rpc/epoch_history.csv); sampled_epochs counts them. upper_bound_share_pct: the same edges from supply alone, counting rewards left unminted as burn. Epoch rows list each sampled epoch. bq_gross_fee_burn_per_day_near: mean BigQuery gross tokens_burnt (sql/fee_burn.sql) over the sampled days in the period. Before the developer gas rebate ended (HSP-027, 2026-11-04) gross overstates the supply burn, because nearcore paid part of function-call gas to the called contract; from then gross equals net. Cross-check only.
